pause_all.label: Pause all driver activity
pause_all.desc: Jobs keep their place and run when this is turned off.

options.report: Report only: log what would be deleted

deletion_mode.label: Delete paused services after their retention period

warning_days.label: Warn customers this many days before deletion

breach_retention_days.label: Delete a service suspended for breach after this many days
breach_retention_days.desc: Counted from the day the hold was set, and only when deletion above is On. Otherwise you get an alert when the days are over.

delete_data.label: Delete the settings when the plugin is deleted
delete_data.desc: This also deletes the plugin's clusters, nodes, connections and other options, and its usage, credit, OAuth and MCP tables. The IP pool, virtual machine records, private network records and hosting records are deleted only when no service that is not deleted still exists, and the DNS assignments only when no name may still point at our servers; otherwise those tables are kept. Machines whose records are deleted can no longer be matched to their services.

currency_guard_rates.label: Guard rates
currency_guard_rates.desc: One line per extra currency you sell in, for example DKK=7.60: how many units of it are worth one euro, a little above the real rate (about 2 percent). Only used to check that an order covers what a supplier is paid in euro (domains, certificates, licence keys); it is never shown or charged to a customer. Without a line for a currency, such an order is refused and you get an alert.

mcp_enabled.label: Let customers connect apps (Use with Claude)
mcp_enabled.desc: Turns the OAuth server and the MCP endpoint on or off for the whole site. Off, connected apps stop working at once. Personal API tokens are not affected.

mcp_redirect_uris.label: Redirect addresses apps may use
mcp_redirect_uris.desc: One address per line, matched exactly. An app can only register and sign in with an address on this list. Empty means the Claude addresses.

api_docs_url.label: API documentation page
api_docs_url.desc: Address of a public page that holds the shortcode [beltoft_services_api_reference]. When set, the Security section in My Account links to it instead of printing its own short guide.

account_billing.label: Group the billing pages
account_billing.desc: My Account shows one Billing item instead of Orders, Subscriptions, Payment methods and Addresses, and those pages get a tab bar. Their addresses stay the same.

welcome_servers_url.label: Welcome block: servers link
welcome_servers_url.desc: Address of the page where customers buy a server. A customer with no services sees three starting points in My Account; one without an address is left out.

usage_threshold_new.label: Bill pay as you go early at this amount: new accounts
usage_threshold_new.desc: In the shop's currency. Another currency takes its own amount from the filter beltoft_services_amount_setting; with none there, it has no value. For an account with no paid usage invoice yet. When the unbilled usage reaches it, the usage is charged at once, without waiting for the monthly renewal.

usage_threshold.label: Bill pay as you go early at this amount: other accounts

usage_minimum.label: Minimum amount to charge a card for pay as you go
usage_minimum.desc: In the shop's currency. Another currency takes its own amount from the filter beltoft_services_amount_setting; with none there, it has no value. Including VAT. When the amount left to charge the card for a month is under this, it is carried to the next month's invoice instead. 0 turns this off.

offer_monthly.label: Show the Monthly option for servers and databases
offer_monthly.desc: Off: customers only see pay as you go, and a new server or database added to the cart as a monthly plan is changed to its pay as you go plan when it has one. Email plans, plugin licences, renewals, plan changes of existing subscriptions and orders made in the admin are not touched.

usage_new_limit.label: Pay as you go services before the first paid usage invoice
usage_new_limit.desc: The most services an account may run until a usage invoice has been paid. 0 means no limit.

credit_enabled.label: Account credit for pay as you go
credit_enabled.desc: Customers prepay a balance, without VAT. It is applied first to their Pay as you go usage invoices, which carry the VAT. Off, nothing about credit shows.

credit_renewals.label: Account credit pays renewals
credit_renewals.desc: Credit also pays the renewal orders of subscriptions, before the card is charged. Credit a customer paid for can pay any renewal. Promotional credit (credit codes and grants) pays pay as you go usage and the renewals of products that have the box "Promotional credit can pay orders and renewals" ticked. A renewal whose rest for the card would be under the usage minimum is paid by the card in full. Needs account credit.

credit_checkout.label: Account credit pays orders at checkout
credit_checkout.desc: Credit also pays the first order of a signed-in customer, before the card is charged: the checkout shows the credit and the amount left to pay. Credit a customer paid for can pay any order. Promotional credit pays only products that have the box "Promotional credit can pay orders and renewals" ticked. An order whose rest for the card would be under the usage minimum is paid by the card in full. A card always needs to be there: the checkout still asks for a payment method, and an order with nothing that saves a card (no subscription, no pay as you go) uses credit only when the customer already has a saved card. Top-ups and plan switches are never paid from credit. Needs account credit.

credit_min.label: Smallest top-up
credit_min.desc: In the shop's currency. Another currency takes its own amount from the filter beltoft_services_amount_setting; with none there, it has no value. No VAT is charged on a top-up: the customer pays this amount and all of it is credited.

credit_max.label: Largest top-up
credit_max.desc: In the shop's currency. Another currency takes its own amount from the filter beltoft_services_amount_setting; with none there, it has no value.

gift_credit.label: Account credit as gift cards
gift_credit.desc: Account credit is gift cards of the plugin Beltoft Gift Cards for WooCommerce, handled by the add-on Beltoft Gift Cards Account Credit: a top-up buys a card for the customer, free credit is a free card made in the gift card plugin, and the cards pay checkout orders, renewals and usage invoices (set in the add-on). Credit already on the old ledger is not applied while this is on, so move it to cards first. Needs both plugins to be active; without them this setting does nothing.

site_tag.label: Site tag
site_tag.desc: Written into the description of every virtual machine this site creates. Only machines that carry this tag are ever changed or deleted. Letters, numbers, dots, dashes and underscores. It cannot be changed while machines exist. A cluster cannot go live until this is set; while it is empty the host name of this site is used, for test clusters only.

shutdown_timeout.label: Shutdown timeout in seconds
shutdown_timeout.desc: How long a pause waits for a clean shutdown before the machine is stopped.

task_wait.label: Seconds to wait for one Proxmox task
task_wait.desc: A step waits this long, then keeps the task and checks it again later. Keep it below the PHP time limit of this server.

host_reserve_gb.label: Memory kept free on each node, in GB
host_reserve_gb.desc: A node counts as full when the memory promised to the virtual machines of this site, plus this reserve, reaches the memory of the node. It leaves room for Proxmox itself and for machines this site did not create.

ip_reserve_for_vps.label: Public IP addresses kept for servers
ip_reserve_for_vps.desc: A database with a public IP address is sold out while no more than this many addresses are free, so the last address always stays available to a new server. 0 lets databases take the last one.

db_disk_max_gb.label: Largest database data disk (GB)
db_disk_max_gb.desc: A database variation with extra storage that would make the data disk larger than this is not offered and a switch to it is refused.

db_disk_step_gb.label: Database extra storage step (GB)
db_disk_step_gb.desc: The extra storage of a database variation must be a multiple of this, or it is not offered and a switch to it is refused.

disk_reserve_gb.label: Storage kept free on each node (GB)

capacity_free_memory_percent.label: Alert when real free memory is under (%)
capacity_free_memory_percent.desc: Each night the memory a node really has free (virtual machine nodes, and hosting nodes whose agent reports it) is compared with what this plugin counts as committed. You are mailed when it is under this share. Nothing is stopped: capacity never blocks a sale.

capacity_free_disk_percent.label: Alert when real free disk is under (%)
capacity_free_disk_percent.desc: The same for the disk of a node: you are mailed when the free share of the storage is under this share.

snapshots_enabled.label: Customer snapshots
snapshots_enabled.desc: Let customers take snapshots of their server and roll back to them. Only servers whose disks are all qcow2 get them. Leave it off until the token has the snapshot privileges and the checks on the cluster have passed.

snapshot_free_days.label: Days a free snapshot is kept

snapshot_paid_days.label: Days a snapshot is kept with paid slots

snapshot_max_slots.label: Most snapshots per server
snapshot_max_slots.desc: Free and paid slots together never go above this.

snapshot_expired_email.label: Email when a snapshot expires
snapshot_expired_email.desc: Tell the customer when a snapshot reached the end of its keeping time and was deleted. The emails about a removed disk and fewer slots are always sent.

snapshot_reserve_gb.label: Storage kept free for snapshots (GB)
snapshot_reserve_gb.desc: A snapshot is refused when the storage of the server has less than this free. 0 uses the storage kept free for extra disks.

abuse_cpu.label: High CPU means above this percent

abuse_hours.label: for at least this many hours
abuse_hours.desc: One reading covers about an hour, so the hours are counted over several hourly readings: with 1 hour the first alert comes with the second reading, with 3 hours after about three.

monitor_alerts.label: Customer monitoring emails
monitor_alerts.desc: Email the customer when their server stays down unexpectedly, its disk is nearly full or its CPU stays high. Customers can turn the usage emails off per server; the server down email is always sent.

monitor_disk_urgent_percent.label: Urgent disk alert threshold, percent
monitor_disk_urgent_percent.desc: A second, stronger email when the disk is almost completely full. It is sent once per episode and re-arms five points lower.

monitor_cpu_hours.label: CPU alert after this many hours
monitor_cpu_hours.desc: Counted over several hourly readings, like the abuse check. Re-arms when the CPU falls below 70 percent.

monitor_cooldown_days.label: Days between two CPU emails for one server

traffic_alerts.label: Outgoing traffic alerts
traffic_alerts.desc: Email the alert address when a server sends a lot of traffic for 30 minutes, or ten times its usual hour. The customer is not told and nothing is restricted. Uses the hourly usage reading: no extra call to Proxmox. An alert comes once and re-arms after six quiet hours.

traffic_alert_percent.label: Sustained traffic, percent of the plan speed
traffic_alert_percent.desc: Alert when the outgoing traffic averages above this share of the plan speed limit for 30 minutes.

traffic_alert_mbit.label: Sustained traffic without a plan speed, Mbit/s
traffic_alert_mbit.desc: Used for servers whose plan has no speed limit.

traffic_jump_factor.label: Traffic jump, times the usual hour
traffic_jump_factor.desc: Alert when the last hour is this many times the median hour of the last 7 days. Judged once a day of hours is known.

traffic_jump_floor_mbit.label: Traffic jump floor, Mbit/s
traffic_jump_floor_mbit.desc: A jump under this hourly average is never alerted, so a quiet server going from 0.1 to 2 Mbit/s stays silent.

monitor_db_bans.label: Database ban alert, banned addresses
monitor_db_bans.desc: The admin is told when a database server has this many addresses banned for failed logins. It re-arms when the count falls below it.

traffic_quarantine.label: Connection flood and scan detection
traffic_quarantine.desc: Reads the per-server connection counts the host sends every minute (route flows, signed with BELTOFT_SERVICES_FLOW_SECRET). Report only emails the alert address. Quarantine also blocks the server's outgoing traffic except DNS to the cluster name servers and answers to incoming connections, tells the customer, and stays until an admin lifts it.

flow_sources.label: Addresses the host sends the counts from
flow_sources.desc: IPv4 addresses, separated by commas. A request from any other address is refused.

flow_minutes.label: A signal counts after this many minutes in a row

flow_scan_dsts.label: Scanning: more than this many different destination addresses

flow_scan_dports.label: Scanning: or more than this many different destination ports

flow_syn_unreplied.label: SYN flood: more than this many connection attempts never answered

flow_udp_dsts.label: UDP flood: more than this many different UDP destinations

hosting_denied_domains.label: Domains customers may not point at hosting
hosting_denied_domains.desc: One domain per line. A domain here, and any name under it, is refused: use it for your own domains (the shop, the mail host, the name servers).

hosting_restore_test.label: Weekly restore test
hosting_restore_test.desc: Once a week one random account backup is restored into a scratch container on the node and checked. Needs a scratch container id on the node.

hosting_order_url.label: Hosting order page
hosting_order_url.desc: Where the Order hosting button in the account goes, for example /wordpress-hosting/#plans. Empty uses the first hosting product page.

hosting_move_url.label: Website move request page
hosting_move_url.desc: A page where a customer asks to have an existing website moved to their hosting, for example /contact/?about=Website move. When set, the hosting account page shows a "Move a website here" panel with a button to it. Empty: no panel.

hosting_move_free.label: The website move is free of charge

hosting_preview_zone.label: Preview zone
hosting_preview_zone.desc: A domain whose DNS zone this site manages. Every site gets a temporary name <name>.<zone>. Hosting provisioning waits until this is set.

hosting_php_default.label: Default PHP version
hosting_php_default.desc: A new site starts on this version, for example 8.3.

hosting_php_versions.label: PHP versions offered
hosting_php_versions.desc: Versions customers can choose, separated by commas, for example 8.3,8.4,8.5. The end-of-support dates are kept with the plan notes.

hosting_php_eol.label: PHP end of support dates
hosting_php_eol.desc: Version and the last day of security support, for example 8.3=2027-12-31,8.4=2028-12-31. Customers are told 90 and 30 days before, and on that day their site moves to the default version.

hosting_prefix.label: Account name prefix
hosting_prefix.desc: Letters and numbers. The account name is this prefix and the license resource id; it names the container, the database user and the edge entry.

hosting_tag.label: Container tag
hosting_tag.desc: A Proxmox tag put on every hosting container. Lowercase letters, numbers and dashes.

hosting_admin_user.label: Default WordPress admin user
hosting_admin_user.desc: The administrator name of a new WordPress install when the order named none.

hosting_mem_overcommit.label: Memory overcommit
hosting_mem_overcommit.desc: Memory promised to containers may be this many times the memory of a node (1 to 4). Set it from load test results.

hosting_disk_overcommit.label: Disk overcommit
hosting_disk_overcommit.desc: Disk promised to containers may be this many times the real disk of a node (1 to 5), on thin storage.

hosting_reserve_gb.label: Memory reserve per node, in GB
hosting_reserve_gb.desc: Kept free for the node system, its cache, the edge and the shared database server.

hosting_alert_percent.label: Capacity alert at, percent
hosting_alert_percent.desc: The admin is told when committed memory or disk on a node reaches this share.

hosting_db_account_cpu.label: Database monitor: one account above, percent of CPU
hosting_db_account_cpu.desc: Alert when one account uses more than this share of the shared database server for the minutes below.

hosting_db_total_cpu.label: Database monitor: server above, percent of CPU
hosting_db_total_cpu.desc: Alert when the shared database server stays above this CPU share for the minutes below.

domain_nameservers.label: Name servers
domain_nameservers.desc: Comma separated host names. Leave empty to disable automatic zones.

domain_price_overrides.label: Price overrides
domain_price_overrides.desc: One extension and its yearly price excluding tax per line, for example com=15 or dk=95.20 (a dot, at most two decimals). A line that cannot be read stops the save.

domain_renew_days_before.label: Charge renewals before expiry, in days

domain_free_transfers.label: Free transfers
domain_free_transfers.desc: For an extension the registrar moves without a year (a transfer price of 0 in its last price answer), the customer pays nothing when the transfer is ordered. The first yearly payment falls on the domain's renewal date, and no year is bought at the registrar before that payment. A customer can move a domain in and cancel before then: the move costs nothing, so the cost is support time only. Off: the transfer is charged as one year, as before.

domain_relock_days.label: Lock an unlocked domain again after, in days
domain_relock_days.desc: A domain left unlocked for transfer is locked again after this many days. 0 turns it off. Turn it on only once you have confirmed how the registrar reports an outgoing transfer, because a transfer under way must not be locked.

domain_seller_name.label: Seller name in the .dk agreement
domain_seller_name.desc: The company that is paid for the registration, as named in the .dk checkout agreement. Empty uses the site name.

domain_infrastructure_zones.label: Own zones on the DNS server
domain_infrastructure_zones.desc: Comma separated zones that belong to the site itself, for example its name server domain. The orphan zone check skips them.

domain_dns_primary_query_address.label: Primary DNS query address
domain_dns_primary_query_address.desc: Local IP address used to check the first name server when its public address cannot be reached from this server.

domain_dns_claims_enabled.label: DNS hosting for domains registered elsewhere
domain_dns_claims_enabled.desc: Customers can verify a domain with a TXT record and add DNS hosting for it. Needs at least two name servers below.

domain_search_url.label: Domain search page
domain_search_url.desc: The address of the page where customers search for and register a domain, for example /domains/. The account shows a Register a domain button when it is set. Leave empty to hide the button.

ssl_enabled.label: Sell SSL certificates
ssl_enabled.desc: Off: certificate orders are refused at checkout and nothing is ordered at the registrar. The registrar account and mode are set under Domains.

ssl_renew_days_before.label: Charge renewals before expiry, in days
ssl_renew_days_before.desc: The registrar renews an order only within 30 days of its expiry, so this is at most 30.

ssl_wait_days.label: Cancel an order that is not validated after, in days
ssl_wait_days.desc: The registrar order is cancelled and staff are told to refund the customer.

ssl_refund_days.label: Refund window after issue, in days
ssl_refund_days.desc: A customer can cancel inside this window. Match the registrar, which refunds within 30 days of issue.

licence_items.label: Licence key items
licence_items.desc: One licence key and Openprovider item per line, for example kernelcare=ITEM-ID-1M. The key is an edition (admin, pro, host, or admin-physical, pro-physical, host-physical) or an add-on (cloudlinux-solo, imunify360-1 and so on). The item is the id from the licence item list, not the price list SKU.

licence_costs.label: Licence key costs
licence_costs.desc: One licence key and what Openprovider charges per month in EUR excluding VAT, for example pro-physical=25.49. A key is only ordered when the paid line covers this. Empty means unknown, and the live client refuses to order.

options.live: Live: call the mail server (also needs BELTOFT_SERVICES_MAIL_LIVE in wp-config.php)

mail_api_url.label: Mail server API address
mail_api_url.desc: The https address of the mailcow web interface, without a path.

mail_api_key.label: Mail server API key
mail_api_key.desc: A read-write mailcow API key that is allowed from this server only. It is stored encrypted and never shown again.

mail_host.label: Mail host name
mail_host.desc: The name customers point their MX records and their mail programs at, for example mail.example.com. Nothing is provisioned until it is set.

mail_order_url.label: Email order page
mail_order_url.desc: Where the Create an email domain button in the account goes, for example /mail/#pricing. Empty uses the product page.

mail_guide_url.label: Setup guide URL
mail_guide_url.desc: Address of a public page that holds the shortcode [beltoft_services_mail_setup]. When set, the Connect tab links to it. Empty means no link.

mail_dav_url.label: Calendar and contacts address
mail_dav_url.desc: The CalDAV and CardDAV address of the mail server, for example https://mail.example.com/dav/. When set, the setup guide and the Connect tab explain how to add the calendar and the contacts. Empty hides them.

mail_reserved_domains.label: Domains customers may not add
mail_reserved_domains.desc: One domain per line. A domain here, and any name under it, is refused: use it for the mail domains the mail server carries for you.

mail_allow_external_forward.label: Let aliases forward to other domains

mail_restart_sogo.label: Restart the calendar and contacts service after a new domain is added
mail_restart_sogo.desc: Sends restart_sogo with each new domain, as the mail server's own Add domain and restart SOGo does. Without it, calendar and contacts of a new domain work only after the next SOGo restart.

mail_spf_include.label: SPF include name
mail_spf_include.desc: The name in include:<name> of the SPF record, a TXT record of your own that lists the mail server addresses. Empty uses the mail host name.

mail_dmarc_rua.label: DMARC report address
mail_dmarc_rua.desc: Where DMARC reports for customer domains go. Empty: the WordPress admin email.

mail_rl_minute.label: Messages per domain per minute
mail_rl_minute.desc: The limit for all mailboxes of one email domain together, set on the mail server when the domain is made and when its plan changes. 0 turns it off.

mail_rl_day.label: Messages per mailbox per day
mail_rl_day.desc: The limit of each mailbox, set when the mailbox is made. 0 turns it off. The mail server blocks sending at the limit; nothing is paused by this plugin.

mail_quota_alert_percent.label: Alert when a mailbox is this full, in percent

console.label: Customer server console
console.desc: Show a browser console for running servers. Keep this off until the console proxy and its permissions have been configured and checked.

plesk_items.label: Plesk licence items
plesk_items.desc: One tier key and Openprovider item per line, for example pro=PLESK-12-VPS-WEB-PRO-1M. The three Plesk for VPS items (admin, pro, host) are used when a tier is not listed.

plesk_costs.label: Plesk licence costs
plesk_costs.desc: One tier key and what Openprovider charges per month in EUR excluding VAT, for example pro=12.50. A licence is only ordered when the paid line of the tier covers this. Empty means unknown, and the live client refuses to order.
